questions.q: Which quadrant should take up most of your working time?
a: Work that is neither urgent nor important
questions.why: Lesson 1 says Q2, where preparation and real work live, deserves the largest share.

questions.q: Checking email is used as an example of which quadrant?
questions.why: Lesson 1 lists email under Q3 and social media under Q4.

questions.q: What does a role statement describe?
a: Where you want to be in your work
The tasks you must finish today
The people who report to you
questions.why: Lesson 2 pairs a role title, the work category, with a role statement about your aim.

questions.q: What three sources of energy does the summary say you must nourish?
questions.why: Lesson 3 lists meaningful purpose, the body and relationships as the energy sources.

questions.q: Why is a time management system useless without self-care?
a: Burnout and poor health make consistency impossible
Rest takes time away from important tasks
Systems only work for disciplined people
Energy matters less than the right software
questions.why: Lesson 3 argues no system survives if your body and energy give out.
